reconciler_notes: RQ1.4: Revision after adversary challenges. Sixteen groups, one past the size guide, by design: RC-01 was partly accepted and the service URL and connection codes (A-FU-10, B-FU-12) were taken out of the server-facing group, because they share no unit with any of its other members and a coder asked 'what was implemented' separates a declaration or config file from code that opens a connection to a remote service. The rest of RC-01 was rejected: A-FU-13 stays with C-FU-06 on U254, where both codes quote the same attribution of the Terraform resource and both definitions name declarative config. Remaining forced calls and residual strain: (1) Numeric, geometric and string-scanning routines are one group because B-FU-16, B-FU-22 and C-FU-01 already lump them and only A split them; the small conversions (B-FU-08, C-FU-03: U024, U125, U057) were absorbed there rather than given a group, which is still the weakest join in this plan, and U024 is the one unit the computation and collection groups genuinely share (RC-02: the earlier claim of a U079/U144 overlap was false and is withdrawn). (8) The provenance group (A-FU-25) now records only unit-supported relations, to U048 and U049; the interpretive link to wrong suggestions is stated in its exclude line, not as a relation (RC-03). | RQ1.5: Seventeen groups, all RQ1.5, after answering six challenges: one accepted outright (RC-06, a relation change), five accepted in part. Unresolved: (1) G08 sits at exactly min_support (U036, U047, U057) and U047 doubles with G05, so a gate may prefer to fold it; the overlap is recorded. (2) C-BE-18 (24 units) is read as a benefit only by C and most of its units are failure reports elsewhere, so the works-here-but-not-there framing may double with the problems question. (3) G11 now mixes praise and astonishment; the adversary would split them, and C's own file did, so a gate wanting a 17th group has the evidence for it (C-BE-12's four units: U002, U017, U024, U144). (4) Four quarantined codes (QA-02, QB-01, QB-02, QC-02) are not benefit codes at all and have no equivalent group here. | RQ2.2: Twenty groups after reconciliation, up from eighteen and further above the 5-15 target. Two challenges were accepted and each adds a group: RC-02 split malformed output (G19: one line, repeated comment, unclosed insertion) out of the wrong-code group, on near-zero unit overlap (jaccard 0.038) and on both A and C having written that boundary into their own exclude clauses - the plan's earlier notes had already flagged this as the first group to split; RC-04 split substitute-naming (G20) out of the vendor-and-roadmap group, which had rested on a single shared unit.
